name: Blattner (Quanta Services)
employees: Not disclosed (aggregator bands 1,000-5,000; 2,000+ deployed on SunZia alone)
ownership: subsidiary of Quanta Services (NYSE: PWR) — acquired Oct 13, 2021 for ~$2.7B (~$2.36B cash + ~$340M stock + up to $300M earnout over 2022-2024; earnout tracked at roughly half of max per fair-value disclosures). Structure: Blattner Company parent → Blattner Energy, Inc. + D.H. Blattner & Sons, Inc.; family-led since 1907 (4th-generation CEO Scott Blattner)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Blattner is the biggest and most opaque construction force in US renewables — a 118-year-old Avon, Minnesota firm claiming to have built >20% of US utility-scale wind, solar and storage (75,000+ MW, 450+ projects, 27,000+ turbines, 3,300+ storage containers, 5.4+ GWh of BESS), now the renewables engine inside Quanta Services' Electric Infrastructure Solutions segment (segment revenue $7.85B in its last standalone year; Quanta FY2025 revenue $28.5B, record $53.4B backlog). It discloses almost nothing — no customers on project pages, no award PRs, essentially never co-named with BESS integrators — so its record must be triangulated: SunZia (3.5+ GW, the largest US clean-energy project, fully online Jun 2026), Slate (where it installed Canadian Solar SSES/e-STORAGE containers — direct proof it builds China-linked BESS), Eleven Mile (Fluence cubes feeding Meta's Mesa data center, attribution vendor-side), and repeat frameworks with Pattern, RWE, Ørsted, Recurrent/Goldman, and NextEra/FPL. The channel truth: owners furnish the batteries on Blattner sites; Blattner's 3,300+ containers make it the deepest containerized-install labor base any US-market OEM must be compatible with.
ecosystemRole: We assess Blattner as the physical backbone of the buyer tier's build programs and the strongest expression of the owner-furnished procurement norm: it advertises 'battery procurement and installation' but every documented project shows the owner picking the integrator (Ørsted↔Fluence, Canadian Solar↔its own SSES, NextEra self-integrating). Inside Quanta, it is one arm of an increasingly integrated AIDC power package — Cupertino Electric (20M+ sq ft of data centers electrified) does inside-the-fence, Blattner builds the generation/storage, Quanta's 2026 acquisitions (Phalcon, Enerfab et al.) deepen mission-critical scope, and the flagship proof is Eleven Mile: (attributed) Blattner-built solar+storage whose majority offtake feeds Meta's Mesa AI campus. For a Chinese OEM the read is sober: Quanta's corporate narrative showcases domestic-content projects and hyperscaler relationships — it will not champion a §154-named supplier — but the Slate precedent shows Blattner installs whatever bankable owners buy.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale wind EPC (the historic franchise)
productsAndServices.description: First contractor globally past 20 GW of wind (2013); 27,000+ turbines; 300+ wind projects / 49+ GW at the 2021 acquisition. Flagship: SunZia Wind (Pattern Energy) — turnkey EPC for 3,515+ MW, 674 GE Vernova turbines, 10 substations, 100+ miles of gen-tie; construction from Sep 2023, fully online Jun 18, 2026 — the largest clean-energy infrastructure project in US history. Other landmarks: Western Spirit (1,050 MW NM), Kern County Wind (1,547 MW), Weatherford (998 MW OK), Taylor/Nolan repower (770 MW TX).
productsAndServices.positioning: Arguably the #1 US wind constructor by fleet — no peer matches the wind franchise; ENR/SPW rankings show Quanta affiliates #1 in US solar installs (10.1 GW + 4.3 GWh storage in 2024 ≈ ~20% of the US solar market; 6.1+ GW in 2025).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Repeat-owner frameworks (Pattern, RWE, Ørsted, Recurrent/Goldman, Entergy, FPL/NextEra) — Blattner announces almost nothing itself; growth shows up only in Quanta segment backlog.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Top-tier developers and utilities at mega-project scale.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Wind-heavy heritage in a storage-led market — the storage practice is the growth vector.

productsAndServices.name: Solar + storage EPC
productsAndServices.description: 90+ solar projects / 12+ GW at acquisition, far more since (Quanta affiliates 10.1 GW installed in 2024 alone); 11 years of utility-scale storage experience, 5.4+ GWh and 3,300+ containers installed. Documented storage builds: Slate (Recurrent → Goldman Sachs Renewable Power; 390 MW solar + 140.25 MW/561 MWh on Canadian Solar SSES/e-STORAGE integration, 2020-22, D.H. Blattner & Sons constructing); Eleven Mile Solar Center (Ørsted — 300 MW solar + 300 MW/1,200 MWh on ~2,000 Fluence cubes, COD Oct 2024, majority offtake to Meta's Mesa AZ data center; Blattner attribution via vendor case study); Emily Solar (RWE, 273.6 MW IL, ribbon-cut May 2026); Andrews County (520 MW TX); plus early BESS (Northern Illinois 20 MW frequency regulation; New Orleans 500 kW pilot).
productsAndServices.positioning: Storage services span site development, foundations, 'battery procurement and installation,' controls, substations, transmission, commissioning, and O&M — but the documented pattern on every named project is owner-furnished batteries.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same repeat-owner frameworks; RWE explicitly cites 'Blattner's delivery credibility.'
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sep 2025 Built Robotics contract (autonomous solar construction) signals productivity push; storage attach on the solar franchise is the organic growth line.

productsAndServices.name: Quanta integration (the AIDC package)
productsAndServices.description: Since Q1 2025 Blattner reports inside Quanta's Electric Infrastructure Solutions segment (FY2025 segment revenue $23.0B; renewables no longer separable — last standalone segment year FY2024: $7.85B revenue, 8.5% operating margin, record $8.72B backlog). Quanta's data-center thesis: $2.4T TAM through 2030 across converging utility/generation/large-load markets; Cupertino Electric (acquired Jul 2024, ~$1.5B — 20M+ sq ft of data centers electrified) plus 2026 additions (Phalcon, Enerfab, Percheron, PSD) build the mission-critical bench; Blattner is the utility-scale generation/storage construction arm of the package.
productsAndServices.positioning: The only US contractor family combining #1 T&D, #1 renewables construction, and top-tier data-center electrical — the integrated grid-to-rack offer hyperscalers increasingly buy.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Quanta's enterprise relationships; hyperscaler-linked builds surface via owner PRs (Eleven Mile → Meta).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers and the utilities serving them.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Quanta FY2026 guidance $39.3-39.7B revenue; record $53.4B backlog (Q2 2026).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Blattner as install infrastructure, not a procurement door: owners furnish the batteries on its sites, it announces nothing, and its value to a BESS OEM is compatibility — container handling, foundation and spacing standards, termination and commissioning interfaces — across the deepest containerized-install labor base in the country (3,300+ containers).

(High confidence) We assess the Quanta context as tilting the account away from Chinese suppliers: the corporate narrative showcases domestic-content stacks (Eleven Mile's First Solar/Fluence/Nextracker feeding Meta) and a $2.4T data-center TAM thesis, and hyperscaler procurement screens are strictest exactly where Quanta is growing. Blattner will not advocate for a §154-named OEM into those accounts.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Slate precedent as the meaningful counterweight: Blattner demonstrably installs China-linked BESS (Canadian Solar SSES) when the owner buys it — there is no blanket China refusal at the EPC level, only owner-level economics and politics. Safe-harbored equipment and non-ITC merchant projects remain constructible.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the opacity itself as strategically informative: a company that builds ~a fifth of US renewables while disclosing nothing runs on long-cycle repeat-owner relationships (Pattern, RWE, Ørsted, NextEra) — the realistic entry is being specified by one of those owners once, after which Blattner's install familiarity becomes a repeatable asset across the whole framework.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: track Quanta's SPW storage volume (4.3 GWh/yr and growing) as the denominator of US BESS construction, treat Blattner compatibility as a qualification checkbox to clear via documentation and training rather than a sales pursuit, and watch the Eleven Mile pattern — solar+storage built for hyperscaler offtake — as the project archetype where Chinese content is least welcome.
